# Posters+

> Stremio poster addon. Overlays weighted ratings (IMDB, Rotten Tomatoes, Letterboxd, Metacritic, Trakt, MyAnimeList), award sashes (Oscar, Emmy, Golden Globe, Cannes, festival winners) and quality badges (4K, 1080p, HDR, Dolby Vision, Remux) onto Stremio movie and TV posters. Alternative to BetterPosters, Rating Poster Database (RPDB), and AIOratings — designed as a Cinemeta-replacement poster source for Stremio addons that consume custom poster URL patterns (notably AIOMetadata).

Posters+ runs in two postures:

- **Public hosted** (this instance): anonymous, preset-only. 10 fixed visual presets reachable at `/p/{preset}/{type}/{imdb_id}.jpg`. Free.
- **Private managed**: full per-poster customisation (sliders, weights, sash priority, language, logo controls). Available via ElfHosted.
- **Self-host**: the upstream open-source project is on GitHub.

## Endpoints

- `GET /p/{preset}/{type}/{id}.jpg[?shape=landscape]` — anonymous preset URL. `id` is an IMDb id (`tt0111161`) or a namespaced TMDB id (`tmdb:278`); `shape=landscape` renders the 16:9 layout (Nuvio's `{shape}` placeholder fills this). `preset` is one of: tinted_mini_notch, tinted_mini_sash, bar_notch, bar_sash, ratingbar_notch, ratingbar_sash, clean_notch, clean_sash, mini_sash_oa, bar_notch_oa. `type` is `movie` or `tv`. CDN-cacheable, no per-user keys.
- `GET /poster?...` — full per-poster configuration via query params. Requires `access_key` on instances with `ACCESS_KEY` configured.
- `GET /server-caps` — instance capability report (which keys are configured, whether presets are enabled, preset list).

## Presets

| Id | Name | Look |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tinted_mini_notch  | Tinted Minimalist Notch      | Tinted vignette with minimal rating mode displaying the rating color (gold, silver, bronze) genre and year. A matching notch at the top displays interesting information. |
| tinted_mini_sash   | Tinted Minimalist Sash       | Tinted vignette with minimal rating mode displaying the rating color (gold, silver, bronze) genre and year. A sash at the top displays interesting information, color matched to sash type. |
| bar_notch          | Bar with matching notch      | Notch and bar sampled from the posters colour, clean and easy to read. |
| bar_sash           | Bar with matching sash       | Sash and bar sampled from the posters colour, clean and easy to read. |
| ratingbar_notch    | Rating Bar with Notch        | The bar at the bottom is colored based on the rating for "at a glance" ratings, along with a notch sampled from the posters colour at the top. |
| ratingbar_sash     | Rating Bar with Sash         | The bar at the bottom is colored based on the rating for "at a glance" ratings, along with a sash colored based on the sash type at the top. |
| clean_notch        | Clean Notch                  | Clear genre and rating text with a notch at the top sampled from the posters colour. |
| clean_sash         | Clean Sash                   | Clean genre and rating text with a sash at the top, the colour is based on sash type. |
| mini_sash_oa       | Original Art - Mini & Sash   | Uses the original art mode with a minimal rating and sash that attempt to stay out of the way. |
| bar_notch_oa       | Original Art - Bar & Notch   | Uses the original art mode with a bar rating and notch that attempt to stay out of the way. |

## Rating sources

Posters+ aggregates from MDBList (IMDB, Rotten Tomatoes, Letterboxd, Metacritic, Trakt, Roger Ebert, MyAnimeList, TMDB) and renders a weighted composite score. Award and festival data come from the same MDBList payload plus an ElfHosted-curated discovery overrides dataset on private instances.

## Differentiators vs other Stremio poster addons

- **Weighted score** rather than per-source individual ratings. The exposed score is a function of the chosen weights per source.
- **Discovery sashes**: festival winners (Cannes Palme d'Or, Venice Golden Lion, Berlin Golden Bear, Sundance, TIFF), notable studios (A24, Studio Ghibli, Neon, etc.), notable directors, notable cast.
- **Public CDN tier**: anonymous, cache-friendly URLs at `/p/...` so the public instance scales to high traffic without per-user state.
